Consumer & Culture Trends

Sustainable Fashion Tech

Technologies, such as recycled materials, digital sampling, and supply chain tracking, aimed at reducing fashion's environmental impact.

Explanation

Sustainable fashion tech covers a range of applications including biofabricated or recycled textiles, 3D digital garment sampling that reduces physical waste during design, blockchain-based supply chain tracking for material sourcing claims, and resale or rental platforms enabled by digital inventory systems. It responds to consumer and regulatory pressure on the fashion industry, one of the most resource-intensive consumer sectors, to reduce waste and improve transparency. For marketers, it is both a genuine product differentiator and an area where unverified or exaggerated sustainability claims carry real reputational and legal risk, known as greenwashing.

Usage context / examples

An apparel brand might use a digital 3D sampling tool to cut the number of physical prototypes made per garment, then market the reduced material waste as part of its sustainability story.

Related terms

Greenwashing, circular fashion, supply chain transparency
